approachQuestion.prompt:
One removal boundary. Return the smallest index i whose strict left sum equals its strict right sum, or -1. The value at i belongs to neither sum.

Input: a=[2,-1,4,1]. Output: 2.

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; -1000000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000000. Signed values are allowed and totals fit 64 bits.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: First sum the entire array. Scan with left=0; at i compare left with total-left-a[i], returning the first match. After testing, add a[i] to left.
options.feedback: The total splits into strict left, current element and strict right. Testing before accumulation excludes the pivot.

options.text: Compare left with total-left, then add the current value.
options.feedback: For [1,3,1], index 1 is valid, but this comparison includes the pivot in the right side and misses it.

options.text: For every index separately rescan all values to its left and right.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

details: First sum the entire array. Scan with left=0; at i compare left with total-left-a[i], returning the first match. After testing, add a[i] to left.
At index i, the right sum is total-left-a[i], excluding the candidate itself. Test before adding a[i] to left. Scanning left to right makes the first successful boundary the required smallest index.

“First sum the entire array. Scan with left=0; at i compare left with total-left-a[i], returning the first match. After testing, add a[i] to left.”: The total splits into strict left, current element and strict right. Testing before accumulation excludes the pivot.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the method in the reveal. Choose its tightest worst-case time and worst-case auxiliary-space pair. Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

options.text: O(log n) time; O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two full passes need only scalar totals and an index.
details: Two passes cost O(n); only total, left and indices are stored.
Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

The first pass reads n values to compute total; the second tests up to n candidate indices using constant-time subtraction and comparison. Two sequential passes give O(n), not O(n²). Recomputing both sides independently per candidate would cause quadratic work. O(log n) is insufficient for this fixed scan: arbitrary signed input supplies no ordered predicate permitting half elimination.

Only total, the running strict-left sum, the candidate index, and fixed temporary values are retained, giving O(1) auxiliary space. The O(n)-space choice would describe building an extra prefix/suffix array, which this method does not allocate. Supplied readings and the returned scalar index are excluded.
